points: Yechezkel is told to face the mountains of Eretz Yisrael and prophesy about them. That is where the people built their idols, and the mountains were dotted with every kind of avodah zarah.
This prophecy is unusual. We usually hear that other nations' idols will be destroyed, but here it is the idols of Bnei Yisrael, and their corpses will be thrown before those idols.
Yechezkel lives in Bavel. Unlike Yirmiyahu, his job is not to get the people in Eretz Yisrael to change, but to teach the exiles what to do when they watch evil people suffer.
Four times the perek says "you will know that I am Hashem." When we see this destruction, we must not gloat. We should let it strengthen our faith that Hashem runs the world.
Hashem tells Yechezkel to strike his hands and stamp his feet: they deserve it, but it is still painful. Rabbi Motzen says we must see Hashem's justice and still feel broken by others' suffering.
